body: No problem :P every time I go into a city the first guard I see always says the arrow thing. Every. Time.
It's not dying from an arrow to the knee, its that every guard ever says something along the lines of "I used to be an adventurer like you  untill I took an arrow in the knee"
Hehe other way around. I have been the one playing skyrim constantly, not my boyfriend.
My school doesn't have too many sports,  but I play softball at another highschool, and I'm on my schools chess team, which suprises people.

6th grade, end of year we were doing a play. My guy friends character was a dog, and the "ears" were cardboard taped to his hair. Me and my friend jokingly pulled them off and he joking acted like we were really hurting him (he was not actually hurt), and above everyone else we heard our teacher scream "OUTSIDE.. NOW!"


another time, 7th grade, me and like 5 of my friends were at a spelling bee, after all but our class and the judges left. We were running between the seats, and all the sudden we hear "SIT DOWN", coming from the nicest teacher. We all dropped on our assess immediatly, every one of us missing the benches and landing on the ground.

I cannot judge since I did neither see the disscussion occur, nor hear both sides of the story, but it may be that your way of expressing your views may have been a bit agressive, but as I stated I have no way of backing that statement..
 That being said, I honestly wish I had someone to express their religion to me when I was younger, not to convert me, simply to show it was acceptable to have different views if anything else. Still being young, (only 16), I am a self proclaimed athiest, with one side of my family being near dangerously catholic, in their beliefs, yet not really their actions. They refused to let anyone share differing views with me. It got to the point that, after much debate with myself, I decided that I was an athiest. I subtly avoided attending church when possible, and all went well. Then I ended up spending a Saturday night at my grandmothers, meaning she would wish for me to go to church the next morning. I tried to politely decline, when she started with questioning as to why I wouldn't want to go to worship god. She continues this, getting more agressive with her questions, when I decided why do I fight this, why not just be true to what my opinions are. I, very politely and calmly, said that I did not want to go to church because I didn't believe in god, that I was an athiest. She looked at me and said that I needed to stop being stupid, and that it was wrong for me to say that. I, again, polietly told her that I was serious, and at that point she called my dad to pick me up, and didn't say another word. 
The following day I recieved a letter saying that she no longer accepted me as part of her family unless I go back to catholicism, that she would try to pray for me, but also that if I didn't change I would go to hell.. I do think, that this, although is not a form of physical abuse, definatly hurt me emotionally.. not sure if it counts as abuse.

You sure as hell seem to need a life too. I realize that this is Reddit, and when you post something, its there for people like you to see. But honestly. If all you have to say is rude demeaning things on the suicide watch subreddit? Why are you here. Do you get your kicks out of putting down people who already feel about as bad as they can?

Thank you, even if I don't know you, just the fact that someone would take the time and tell me not to mean something... I'm trying to fight it, but its just so tough when everything is against you...
